title: Flávio Bolsonaro Leads Quaest Poll in 2nd Round
seoTitle: Flávio Bolsonaro Leads Quaest Poll in 2nd Round
subtitle: Poll Reveals Technical Tie and Shifts in Specific Segments
excerpt: The Quaest poll, released on September 14, shows Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of Lula with 42% against 40%, marking his first numerical advantage since April.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The Quaest poll, commissioned by Globo and the newspaper O Globo, revealed on September 14 that Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads Lula (PT) in the 2nd round with 42% against 40%, marking his first numerical advantage since April. The survey, which interviewed 2,004 people aged 16 or older nationwide between September 10 and 13, has a margin of error of two percentage points and a confidence level of 95%.

Technical Tie and Variations by Gender

  • Women: Lula 41%, Flávio 38% (3-point difference)
  • Men: data not specified in the source

Age and Income Segments

  • 16 to 34 years old: Flávio 43%, Lula 37% (6-point difference)
  • 35 to 59 years old: Flávio 44%, Lula 39% (5-point difference)
  • 60 years or older: Lula 45%, Flávio 39% (6-point difference)
  • Above 2 minimum wages up to 5 minimum wages: Flávio 46%, Lula 36% (10-point difference)
  • More than 5 minimum wages: Flávio 47%, Lula 34% (13-point difference)

Regions and Ethnic Groups

  • Southeast: Flávio 47%, Lula 31% (16-point difference)
  • Central-West/North: Flávio 46%, Lula 37% (9-point difference)
  • Northeast: Flávio 60%, Lula 28% (32-point difference)
  • Mixed-race: Lula 44%, Flávio 38% (6-point difference)
  • White: Flávio 48%, Lula 33% (15-point difference)
  • Black: Flávio 36%, Lula 48% (12-point difference)

Impact of Mobilization and Street Presence

  • According to Sóstenes Cavalcante, leader of the PL, the poll is “delayed” in relation to Flávio's growth, which had already been observed about two weeks prior.
  • The PL reportedly maintained a more intense schedule of events, with four rallies compared to one by the PT, and more noticeable mobilization in the streets.
  • Lula, in turn, reportedly maintained an executive chief's routine, while Flávio was on parliamentary recess, which could influence his availability for rallies.

Balanced Rejection Between Candidates

  • Regarding rejection, 55% of respondents state they would never vote for Lula, and the same percentage rejects Flávio.

With information from G1, Poder360.
